phases.name: Define the feature contract
phases.description: Separate prompt targets from feature semantics, freshness, identity, and the service-level definitions that still need owners.

phases.name: Ingest and compute shared features
phases.description: Keep streaming and batch sources while executing the same versioned transformation contract on both paths.

phases.name: Materialize dual stores and point-in-time data
phases.description: Separate online lookup from offline history and prevent future information from entering training joins.

phases.name: Serve, discover, and monitor
phases.description: Connect model consumers and catalog users through governed APIs, with explicit online and offline access paths.

phases.name: Validate scale and consistency
phases.description: Measure latency, throughput, skew, data quality, and backfill behavior against owner-defined contracts.

steps.title: Read the frozen feature-store brief
steps.content: Design a Feature Store for Machine Learning. Design a feature store that serves features for both training and inference, ensures consistency between offline and online features, handles feature transformations, and provides feature discovery and governance. Functional requirements: Serve features for batch training and online inference; Ensure offline-online feature consistency; Compute features from streaming and batch sources; Support point-in-time correct feature joins; Provide feature discovery and documentation; Track feature lineage and dependencies; Implement feature monitoring and quality checks; Support feature sharing across teams. Non-functional constraints: Online feature serving latency under 10ms; Support 10k+ features across 100+ entities; Handle 100k+ feature requests per second; Zero training-serving skew; Feature backfill within SLA. Hints: Use Feast, Tecton, or custom implementation; Implement dual storage (Redis for online, S3/BigQuery for offline); Use streaming frameworks for real-time feature computation; Implement feature versioning with schema registry; Use materialization jobs for offline-to-online sync; Implement feature statistics monitoring for drift detection. These are supplied workload targets and candidate patterns; they are not evidence that a chosen platform meets them.

steps.title: Ask what feature freshness means
steps.content: Clarify entity keys and ownership, event time versus availability time, late-arrival policy, TTL/freshness by feature, null/default behavior, schema evolution, access-control boundaries, online consistency semantics, latency percentile and measurement boundary, peak/burst request shape, and the backfill SLA. The brief gives 10k+ features, 100+ entities, and 100k+ requests/second, but not cardinality per entity, payload size, update rate, or retention. Do not invent those values.

steps.title: Make transformations a shared, versioned contract
steps.content: One declarative or compiled transformation definition should be exercised by both streaming and batch execution. Persist its code/schema digest with materialized values and training datasets.

decision.question: Should online and offline features have separately maintained transformation implementations?
decision.chosen: Use one versioned feature definition with compatible streaming and batch execution and parity checks.
decision.chosenReason: Independent copies drift silently; a shared contract makes semantic equivalence testable while allowing different compute engines.

alternatives.option: Duplicate transformation logic in each pipeline
alternatives.tradeoff: Easy to start, but code paths can diverge and cause training-serving skew.

alternatives.option: Force one physical engine to serve both batch and online workloads
alternatives.tradeoff: Simplifies code but can compromise either latency, cost, or historical processing needs.

steps.title: Isolate source-specific ingestion
steps.content: Use a custom adapter because the catalog does not include a generic feature-source connector. Normalize entity identity, event/availability timestamps, source, schema version, and quality metadata from streaming and batch sources.

component.label: Feature Source Adapters
component.description: Normalizes streaming and batch source records into governed entity events.

properties.purpose: Normalize source, entity key, event time, availability time, schema version, and quality metadata for both streaming events and batch snapshots.

component.highlightReason: The feature store must accept distinct source modes without losing the timestamps needed for freshness and point-in-time correctness.

steps.title: Buffer continuously arriving source events
steps.content: Use a durable event stream for real-time source updates and replay. Partitioning and retention depend on measured key skew, update rate, and recovery objectives, none of which are specified beyond the request-rate target.

component.label: Feature Source Event Stream
component.description: Durable asynchronous transport for streaming feature inputs.

properties.purpose: Buffer source updates for streaming feature computation and replay with entity identity and event-time metadata; size from measured workload.

component.highlightReason: Streaming feature inputs need a replayable boundary decoupled from compute consumers.

steps.title: Keep versioned source and offline history
steps.content: Use object storage for immutable source snapshots, offline materializations, and dataset manifests. Keep raw records separate from transformed feature versions by prefix/table and schema, even when they share a storage system.

component.label: Offline Feature and Source Lake
component.description: Versioned batch sources, offline feature values, and training manifests.

properties.purpose: Retain versioned batch inputs, offline feature materializations, and reproducible training manifests with schema and transformation provenance.

component.highlightReason: Batch training and backfill need durable, large-scale historical values rather than reads from the online cache.

steps.title: Compute current features incrementally
steps.content: Use event-time state, late-data handling, deduplication, and explicit watermark semantics. Reprocessing a record should be safe and should preserve the feature-definition version used.

component.label: Streaming Feature Compute
component.description: Evaluates versioned transformations over continuously arriving entity events.

properties.purpose: Apply the shared feature definition to event-time records, handle late/duplicate events, and emit feature values with entity, freshness, and definition-version metadata.

component.highlightReason: Streaming sources need incremental computation while preserving semantics and freshness evidence.

steps.title: Compute batch features and backfills
steps.content: Reuse the same transformation contract for scheduled materialization and correction/backfill runs. Checkpoint by source range and feature version so retries are idempotent and partial backfills are visible.

component.label: Batch Materialization and Backfill
component.description: Computes offline features and repairs historical or online materializations.

properties.purpose: Run batch feature computation and backfills using the shared definition, with checkpoints, idempotent writes, progress visibility, and owner-defined SLA tracking.

component.highlightReason: Backfill is explicit but no duration is supplied; resumable jobs expose progress against the agreed SLA.

steps.title: Version definitions separately from execution engines
steps.content: The catalog has no dedicated transform registry, so use a custom logical component for the shared definition and validation contract. Bind entity keys, event-time behavior, units, null handling, schema, and code digest to each feature version.

component.label: Versioned Feature Definitions
component.description: Governed definitions compiled or interpreted by batch and streaming engines.

properties.purpose: Version feature schemas, entity keys, units, time semantics, null behavior, code digest, owners, and compatible streaming/batch execution contracts.

component.highlightReason: One shared semantic definition is the main design control for reducing offline-online skew.

steps.title: Use the catalog Feature Store as the logical boundary
steps.content: The existing canonical feature-store node represents feature definitions and access behavior, not a guarantee of a particular vendor's dual-store implementation. Feast is a possible implementation from the prompt hints; confirm platform fit, entity model, and operational needs before committing.

component.label: Governed Feature Store
component.description: Logical access and materialization boundary for shared feature definitions.

properties.purpose: Expose governed feature definitions and retrieval/materialization semantics for the stated 10k+ feature catalog; platform selection is a proposal to validate against 100+ entities and workload.

component.highlightReason: A catalog-native feature-store component exists, so this guide reuses it rather than inventing a duplicate node type.

steps.title: Route only continuously arriving records to the stream
steps.content: Keep batch snapshots on the durable lake path and streaming events on the broker path; both carry the same entity and time contract.

connection.label: Streaming source updates
connection.description: Normalized, replayable entity events with source and event-time metadata.

steps.title: Capture batch snapshots and source history
steps.content: Write source manifests and schema snapshots so a later training dataset can reproduce the values available at a historical time.

connection.label: Batch snapshots and raw history
connection.description: Versioned source inputs and manifests for offline computation and point-in-time datasets.

steps.title: Process stream partitions incrementally
steps.content: Monitor per-key skew, event age, and consumer recovery time. Request rate alone does not define event volume or the correct partition count.

connection.label: Entity-keyed feature inputs
connection.description: Continuous records consumed with explicit event-time and replay semantics.

steps.title: Read batch ranges for computation and backfill
steps.content: Use bounded manifests and checkpoints so a retry resumes the same feature version and source range instead of creating ambiguous duplicate outputs.

connection.label: Versioned source and backfill ranges
connection.description: Manifest-driven batch input for historical compute, correction, and offline materialization.

steps.title: Apply the shared contract in streaming
steps.content: Pin each running job to a definition digest and expose the deployed version with produced values. Safe rollout should support compatibility checks and rollback.

connection.label: Versioned streaming transform
connection.description: Shared feature definitions, schema, units, time semantics, and validation rules for online computation.

steps.title: Apply the same contract in batch
steps.content: Batch and stream engines may differ, but golden-record parity tests must compare values, nulls, units, and event-time boundaries for the same input and definition version.

connection.label: Versioned batch transform
connection.description: The identical feature definition and schema executed for batch training, replay, and backfill.

steps.phase: Materialize dual stores and point-in-time data
steps.title: Govern schemas, ownership, and lineage
steps.content: Store searchable feature metadata: names, descriptions, entities, types, owners, access grants, dependencies, definition digest, lifecycle, and audit events. Keep large feature values in their data stores.

component.label: Feature Metadata and Lineage Catalog
component.description: Transactional registry for schemas, owners, dependencies, and governance state.

properties.purpose: Index feature definitions, entity schemas, ownership, documentation, access controls, dependencies, versions, lifecycle, and audit history without storing bulk feature values.

component.highlightReason: Discovery, documentation, sharing, lineage, and governance need a searchable control-plane record.

steps.phase: Materialize dual stores and point-in-time data
steps.title: Publish streaming values through the feature contract
steps.content: Write with feature/entity key, event time, availability time, definition version, and freshness. Define dedupe and late-event corrections before declaring offline and online values equivalent.

connection.label: Fresh computed feature values
connection.description: Versioned streaming feature values and timestamps published through the governed store contract.

steps.phase: Materialize dual stores and point-in-time data
steps.title: Publish batch values and resumable backfills
steps.content: Keep run ID, source range, checkpoint, definition version, and destination state visible. Backfill completion time can only be judged after the owner defines the SLA and workload size.

connection.label: Batch materialization and repair
connection.description: Offline/backfill values and online refresh requests with checkpoint and version provenance.

steps.phase: Materialize dual stores and point-in-time data
steps.title: Track materializations against definitions
steps.content: Update catalog state atomically with definition version, job/run status, lineage edges, and last successful materialization. Avoid documenting a feature as ready while its serving value is stale or absent.

connection.label: Definition and lineage metadata
connection.description: Versioned feature schema, owner, upstream dependencies, lifecycle, and materialization status.

steps.phase: Materialize dual stores and point-in-time data
steps.title: Add a purpose-built online value store
steps.content: Use the existing cache component for low-latency online values, keyed by entity and feature with explicit TTL/freshness metadata. Redis is a candidate hinted by the prompt; size, sharding, persistence, and eviction policy require workload measurements.

component.label: Online Feature Values
component.description: Low-latency entity-keyed feature retrieval for inference.

properties.purpose: Serve versioned online feature values by entity/feature key with freshness and definition metadata; persistence, partitioning, capacity, and TTL are workload decisions.

component.highlightReason: The online lookup path needs a separate low-latency store from large offline training history.

steps.phase: Materialize dual stores and point-in-time data
steps.title: Materialize current values into the online store
steps.content: Publish only complete values for the selected definition version. Define atomic multi-feature read semantics and stale/missing behavior; do not silently substitute a value from an incompatible version.

connection.label: Online materialization
connection.description: Current feature values with entity key, feature version, event time, and freshness metadata.

steps.phase: Materialize dual stores and point-in-time data
steps.title: Build point-in-time joins explicitly
steps.content: Use event time and availability time to select only values that were observable at each training prediction timestamp. Enforce entity-key joins and prevent future updates from leaking into historical examples.

component.label: Point-in-Time Training Join
component.description: Produces leakage-resistant training rows from versioned offline feature history.

properties.purpose: Join feature values to prediction examples by entity and as-of timestamp using only values available at that time, with schema and transformation versions recorded.

component.highlightReason: Point-in-time correctness is a named requirement and protects evaluation from future-data leakage.

steps.phase: Materialize dual stores and point-in-time data
steps.title: Read historical feature versions as of the example time
steps.content: Use offline partitions with both event and availability timestamps. If an upstream correction arrives later, preserve when it became known rather than rewriting what a historical model could have seen.

connection.label: Versioned offline history
connection.description: Historical feature values and source manifests with event time, availability time, and transformation version.

steps.phase: Materialize dual stores and point-in-time data
steps.title: Resolve the feature schema used in each join
steps.content: Resolve names, entity types, transformations, ownership, and compatible versions from the catalog; reject missing or incompatible metadata instead of creating a best-effort training set.

connection.label: Feature schema and version map
connection.description: Governed feature definitions and entity schemas resolved for reproducible historical joins.

steps.phase: Materialize dual stores and point-in-time data
steps.title: Feed reproducible datasets to batch training
steps.content: Persist the join query, feature versions, time boundary, and output manifest with each model run. Training should not query the mutable online cache for historical examples.

component.label: Batch Model Training

properties.purpose: Train from immutable point-in-time joined datasets and record the feature, schema, transformation, and source snapshot versions used.

component.highlightReason: Batch training needs reproducible historical data, not online cache snapshots that change during an experiment.

steps.phase: Materialize dual stores and point-in-time data
steps.title: Use only the frozen point-in-time dataset
steps.content: Publish a dataset manifest and quality summary before training starts. Re-running a training job with the same manifest should reproduce the same input data.

connection.label: Frozen training examples
connection.description: Point-in-time correct feature rows and immutable dataset manifest.

steps.phase: Materialize dual stores and point-in-time data
steps.title: Represent an online inference consumer
steps.content: Model-serving is the example online consumer; other services can use the same governed API. Requests should batch features where semantics allow and include entity IDs, requested feature versions, and a request timestamp.

component.label: Online Model Inference
component.description: Consumes fresh online features for prediction requests.

properties.purpose: Request governed online features by entity and feature version, validate response freshness, and record the exact feature values/versions used for inference.

component.highlightReason: A concrete online consumer makes the under-10ms feature path and training-serving parity observable.

steps.title: Expose governed feature and catalog APIs
steps.content: Route online retrieval and discovery through authenticated APIs. Apply tenant/team permissions, request validation, bounded batch sizes, rate limits, and feature-level access policy; the API layer does not itself guarantee 100k requests per second.

component.label: Feature Retrieval and Catalog API
component.description: Authenticated feature reads and discovery/documentation endpoints.

properties.purpose: Expose governed online feature reads and catalog/documentation endpoints with authorization, validation, rate control, and observable request latency; 100k+ requests/second is a load-test target, not a proven capacity.

component.highlightReason: Feature sharing requires a controlled API boundary and the brief explicitly states a high request-rate target.

steps.title: Give teams a place to find and understand features
steps.content: Display description, owner, entity, units, freshness, source dependencies, transformation version, quality status, access policy, and usage examples. Do not list a feature as ready without a current materialization and an accountable owner.

component.label: Feature Discovery Portal
component.description: Searches documented features and exposes ownership and lineage.

properties.purpose: Let teams discover and document shared features, review entity/schema/owner/lineage/freshness/quality metadata, and request access through the governed API.

component.highlightReason: Discovery, documentation, and cross-team sharing are explicit requirements, not incidental metadata fields.

steps.title: Use the same authorization boundary for discovery
steps.content: Apply user/team permissions server-side, not only in the browser. Audit search, access grants, and feature retrieval according to the ownership model.

connection.label: Search, docs, and access requests
connection.description: Authenticated discovery and feature-access workflows through the governed API.

steps.title: Request features through the governed API
steps.content: Keep the feature fetch in the model-serving request path measurable and bounded. Cache immutable definitions separately from mutable online values, and include request tracing for end-to-end latency.

connection.label: Online feature request
connection.description: Authenticated batch lookup for entity-keyed features and required versions.

steps.title: Resolve governed feature definitions
steps.content: The API resolves an authorized feature contract before reading values. Reject unknown, retired, or incompatible versions with an explicit response rather than silently returning another feature.

connection.label: Authorized feature lookup
connection.description: Feature retrieval and catalog requests evaluated against the governed feature definition.

steps.title: Return current values with freshness metadata
steps.content: A cache miss, stale value, or schema mismatch needs explicit caller behavior. Set fallback/timeout semantics with model owners rather than silently substituting offline data on a latency-critical request.

connection.label: Online reads and freshness
connection.description: Low-latency values with observed freshness and definition version returned to the feature access layer.

steps.title: Resolve owners, docs, lineage, and access policy
steps.content: Catalog APIs should support searchable metadata and lineage traversal without scanning the value stores. Record access decisions and dependency changes for audit.

connection.label: Catalog and authorization metadata
connection.description: Indexed documentation, entity schemas, owners, lineage, lifecycle, and team access policy.

steps.title: Observe feature quality and serving behavior
steps.content: Monitor per-feature freshness, missingness, distributions, schema failures, backfill progress, online request latency and rate, cache hit/miss behavior, and parity comparisons between offline and online outputs.

component.label: Feature Quality and Serving Monitor
component.description: Tracks feature freshness, parity, data quality, request load, and materialization health.

properties.purpose: Measure feature freshness and quality, offline-online parity, request rate/latency, cache behavior, schema errors, lineage/materialization status, and backfill SLA progress.

component.highlightReason: Monitoring must detect skew and stale or low-quality features before consumers learn from silent data defects.

steps.title: Measure streaming freshness and data quality
steps.content: Emit source-to-feature age, late-event counts, duplicate rate, null/invalid values, and transformation failures with feature and entity dimensions.

connection.label: Streaming freshness and quality
connection.description: Event lag, event-time lateness, feature freshness, schema errors, and quality distributions.

steps.title: Expose backfill progress against an agreed SLA
steps.content: Report source range completed, checkpoint, retries, failed partitions, destination publication, and estimated completion based on observed throughput. No duration can be judged until the SLA and backfill volume are supplied.

connection.label: Materialization and backfill status
connection.description: Checkpointed progress, failures, retries, publication state, and measured completion time.

steps.title: Measure online latency and value freshness
steps.content: Measure requested feature count and entity distribution as well as p50/p95/p99 latency at the agreed service boundary. The prompt does not specify a percentile, so do not claim the under-10ms target is passed until one is chosen.

connection.label: Online store latency and freshness
connection.description: Lookup timing, hit/miss, payload size, feature version, and observed staleness.

steps.title: Test semantic parity using golden records
steps.content: For identical versioned inputs, compare batch and stream outputs at boundary timestamps, nulls, late data, and schema changes. A zero-skew objective needs an explicit numeric comparison rule and test corpus.

connection.label: Parity and definition health
connection.description: Definition versions, materialization state, offline-online parity samples, and compatibility test results.

steps.title: Load-test the stated feature and request scale
steps.content: The brief explicitly states 10k+ features across 100+ entities and 100k+ requests per second, but not value sizes, entity cardinalities, read/write ratio, or burstiness. Test skewed hot entities, batched and sparse lookups, cold-cache behavior, and concurrent backfill; capacity is not inferred from component properties.

scaleTrigger.metric: Online request rate and latency distribution, hot-key skew, feature count/entity cardinality, cache saturation, and backfill contention
scaleTrigger.action: Load-test representative 10k+ feature and 100+ entity catalogs at the 100k+ request/second target; partition or replicate only after measuring bottlenecks and consistency behavior.
scaleTrigger.impact: Validates the supplied scale and under-10ms goals while ensuring backfill does not starve online inference.

steps.title: Treat zero skew as a testable invariant
steps.content: Shared code alone does not guarantee identical values when timestamps, null handling, engine functions, late data, or defaults differ. Use cross-engine golden tests and compare sampled production values with version identity.

decision.question: Can the feature store promise zero training-serving skew by using one registry?
decision.chosen: Treat zero skew as an invariant to demonstrate for the supported definitions and execution engines, with explicit exceptions and parity monitoring.
decision.chosenReason: A shared definition reduces drift but does not erase differences in execution, time semantics, or source availability.

alternatives.option: Assume one definition means identical outputs
alternatives.tradeoff: Misses runtime, timestamp, missing-value, and engine-function differences.

alternatives.option: Allow independent transformations and compare only aggregate metrics
alternatives.tradeoff: Can conceal per-entity or per-feature mismatches that affect model predictions.

steps.title: Persist offline feature values for training
steps.content: Write transformed offline feature values and their source/definition manifests to durable storage. Keep raw inputs and materialized tables logically isolated, and publish a run only when its manifest and quality checks are complete.

connection.label: Versioned offline materialization
connection.description: Durable feature values and manifests for training, replay, and backfill, separate from raw source snapshots.

steps.title: Review access, lineage, and failure behavior
steps.content: Before rollout, verify team-level feature permissions, ownership and deprecation workflow, complete lineage, offline dataset reproducibility, online stale/missing-value behavior, schema compatibility, backfill recovery, and parity evidence. Agree feature-specific freshness/TTL, backfill completion SLA, late-data correction policy, quality thresholds, latency percentile and measurement boundary, and recovery behavior with platform and model teams. The brief leaves these unspecified; this is an unpublished structural review draft and no AI score, browser persistence, AWS write, or publication is asserted.
